facts.claim: Mikey Mike's Life on Earth: Vol. 1 was released on 30 August 2019 on Trippy Circus. It has 13 tracks and runs about 33 minutes.
Qobuz's credits for the standalone "Life on Earth" single list Mikey Mike as composer, lyricist and producer, and Mark Nolan as an additional producer. The track runs 2:45.
EARMILK premiered "Life On Earth" in March 2019 as the first track from the album. It describes the song as built on acoustic guitar chords and delicate vocals.

Mikey Mike has said the album was made to be loose and raw rather than polished by a big production team. He also said he and his team want to make a TV show called Life on Earth, with each song shaping an episode.
Mikey Mike described the album as a trip through life, from spiritual places to more physical or nasty ones. He told one outlet that Vol. 1 was diverse in genre.

Gigsoup reports that "Life on Earth" and "Strange Times" are among the album's more philosophical tracks. It also says he began the album about five years before release and was signed and then dropped by a label in that time.

"Mikey Mike's Life on Earth" is an ongoing project that he expects to complete over his lifetime and release in volumes. Vol. 1 includes earlier singles such as "Doin' Me", which was used in a Canon commercial.

His official bio says the Life on Earth album roll-out began with "Doin' Me". It describes a series of singles that will make up a complete album only upon his death, and says a scripted TV series of the same name is in the works.

Mikey Mike is the stage name of Mike Williams, a Los Angeles-based singer, songwriter and producer. His debut single "Doin' Me" (2017) was produced by Rick Rubin and promoted with a viral billboard and poster campaign. He produced "Jump" on Rihanna's 2012 album Unapologetic.
He was born in a small town in Maryland. He later moved to Nashville and recorded his second album, Life on Earth, Vol. 2, with Dave Cobb.

research.lineage: Mikey Mike sits in a Los Angeles-based alt-pop and indie scene that mixes pop, rap, R&B and hooky indie rock, and the sources link him to producer Rick Rubin.

draft:
The trouble starts with a math problem: "the more I see / Of life on earth, the more I wanna leave." Mikey Mike sets it up as a simple ratio, the kind of thing you'd say half-joking, and then spends the rest of **Life on Earth** proving he means it. This isn't a breakup song or a bad-day song. It's about a deeper tiredness, a sense that the place itself is wrong, and a stubborn faith that somewhere else must be right.

The chorus carries that faith. "Take me home, take me home" sounds like homesickness, but the home is a place the narrator has never been, only a "better place out there." That's what gives the song its odd tenderness. Exhaustion and hope sit in the same breath, and neither wins. The second verse gets angrier. He's "so damn low," watching psychopaths run the show and get rewarded for it, and the line about how far you'll go curdles into a sneer. Then the bridge drops the anger for something more fragile: "please wake me up from this dream / I think I'm stuck." The next confession is the one that lands hardest. "I been trying, trying to sing" his way out, and the song we're hearing becomes the attempt itself. After that the chorus comes back twice, no answer found, just the plea again.

The band doesn't mope along with him. A drum kit keeps a steady, driving beat with a prominent snare. The bass holds a plain, repeating line, and a clean guitar figure picks out arpeggios around the melody. The groove has a moderate tempo and a slight push to it, so the music keeps moving forward even as the words keep asking to get off. Mikey Mike's voice is clear with a little rasp at the edges, and he sings it straight, no theatrics, which makes the despair sound lived-in rather than performed.

Mikey Mike is the stage name of Mike Williams, a Los Angeles singer, songwriter and producer who produced "Jump" for Rihanna and whose debut single, "Doin' Me," was produced by Rick Rubin. He wrote and produced this one himself, with Mark Nolan as an additional producer. It opened the album *Mikey Mike's Life on Earth: Vol. 1*, a record he started about five years before its release, a stretch in which he was signed and then dropped by a label. He calls the project a trip through life, from spiritual places to nasty ones, and plans to keep adding volumes for the rest of his life. This song is the title-card thesis for all of it.

It sticks because it lets you admit you're worn out on the world without giving up on the idea that a better one is waiting somewhere.
